newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close higher in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close higher in volatile trade.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Tuesday in volatile trading following Wall Street's rise, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.64 percent, or 1.64 points, to 256.50 on all-share turnover of 116 million shekels against 102 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.53 percent higher at 265.27.

"The session opened with nice gains following Wall Street's rise and the indices rose by almost 1.5 percent. Just towards the end of the trading day the market started sliding for no evident reason," said Yoram Ben-Yaeir at Ahrayut Investment Management.

"The market looks very good and I believe that we are at the beginning of a new positive trend. The market has been stuck since mid-January and now its ready for another rise," said Ari Eidelheit at Zeler Eblgon Securities.

Ben-Yaeir was less optimistic, saying the market is not expected to move as long as the political uncertainty continues. "The result of Netanyahu's trip is not clear yet and the market needs more information," he said.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu left Washington on Monday after a tough two-hour meeting with President Bill Clinton failed to revive Israeli-Palestinian peace talks.
"The recovery of the stock market is accompanied by a rise in CPI-linked bonds which indicates that the market awaits another rate cut," Eidelheit added.

Israel Discount Bank said in a report released on Tuesday that interest rates will fall by 0.5 percentage point during the second quarter due to a slowing economy but will hold steady in the third quarter.
Traders noted that shares of export-oriented companies led the rise following the decline of the shekel against the dollar.

Elite Industries plunged 5.0 percent to 8,754 agorot. Traders said Elite fell because investors believe the Strauss family is about to exercise an option to buy out the Federman group stake in the company.
"That's the end of the battle...from now on Strauss has to deal alone with this problematic company," Ben-Yeair said.

The most active shares were Bank Hapoalim, which gained 0.75 percent to 704 agorot on volume of 7.5 million shekels; Koor Industries, which rose 1.5 percent to 31,606 on a turnover of 5.9 million shekels; and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which gained 1.25 percent to 19,132 agorot on turnover of 4.3 million shekels.
